title: lint: twelve field-path rules and two private readers judge object fields without the objectExtensions fold, so a view, report, dataset or page naming an extension-added field is refused
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzfgvGexKn9vLHsy89K

Filing gate: ③ the carried census of #30303 (PR #30359), carried as a follow-up so that PR stays at the one rule the card named. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p2, because the same multi-package artifact that hit #30303 (HotCRM, hotcrm#2315: a module package adds fields to an app package's object through `objectExtensions`) will hit these rules as soon as a view, report, dataset, page or widget names one of those fields. Route: `domain:spec` (packages/lint).

**What an author sees.** The runtime serves an object with every body's `objectExtensions` folded in. These lint rules index the declared objects only, so a field path that names an extension-added field reads as unknown and is refused (or mis-judged), although the served object has the field.

**Why.** PR #30359 adds one shared fold in `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` (`objectExtensionsByTarget`, `objectsAsServed`) that mirrors the registry's merge. The FLS-key check, the controlled-by-parent merge (#23210) and the membership-key check read it. These still read `indexObjectGraph` over declared objects only (census at PR #30359's head, by reading, not reproduced per rule):

- `validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`
- `validate-dataset-references.ts`
- `validate-field-consumers.ts` (its header says extensions are not judged)
- `validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`
- `validate-object-field-refs.ts`
- `validate-page-field-bindings.ts`
- `validate-preset-comparands.ts`
- `validate-report-runtime-filter.ts`
- `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`
- `validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts` (indexes the declared anchor only)
- `validate-thank-you-record-fields.ts`
- `validate-widget-bindings.ts`

Two more read extension fields through private readers of their own:
- `validate-related-list-refs.ts`: the stack's top-level `objectExtensions` only, with no `packages[]` bodies;
- `validate-mapping-target-fields.ts` (`extensionFieldsByTarget`): the top level plus every body, additive, without the registry's one-entry-per-package replacement.

## Wanted

- [ ] Move each rule above onto `objectsAsServed` (or the shared `objectExtensionsByTarget`), one fold for all. For each one, say whether an extension-added field should satisfy it. A rule that judges a security posture on the declared anchor (sharing, RLS) may deliberately stay on declared fields; if so, say why in its header.
- [ ] Retire the two private readers onto the shared fold.
- [ ] A pin per moved rule: an extension-added field passes; a field no body declares or extends is still refused.

Blocked-by: #30303
